original_question: Give a proof, using PDE techniques, of the a priori estimate in Theorem 3.1: if B is the unit ball in C^n, p > 1, phi is a smooth plurisubharmonic function on B with phi|_{partial B} = 0, and det(phi_{j ar{k}}) = f, then ||phi||_{L^infty(B)} <= C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}, where C depends only on n and p.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Question 18 (Blocki–Kołodziej), which asks for a PDE-based proof of the L^∞ estimate stated immediately before in Theorem 3.1.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact local estimate from Theorem 3.1: the unit ball B in C^n, the hypothesis p>1, a smooth plurisubharmonic function φ with zero boundary values, the complex Monge–Ampère equation det(φ_{j\bar{k}})=f, the conclusion ||φ||_{L^∞(B)} ≤ C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}, and the fact that the intended method is PDE-based.
missing_details: The paper’s official research target is not Theorem 3.1 itself but Question 18: to find a proof of that already-known estimate using PDE techniques.
The question should explicitly say that B is the unit ball B ⊂ C^n and that the equation det(φ_{j\bar{k}})=f holds in B.
The notation φ_{j\bar{k}} should be defined as the complex Hessian entries ∂²φ/∂z_j∂\bar{z}_k.
It should explicitly state that f belongs to L^p(B) and that the L^p norm is taken with respect to Lebesgue measure on B.

Since the boundary condition φ|_{∂B}=0 is part of the statement, the formulation should make clear that φ has a boundary trace there (for example, by assuming φ is continuous on \bar{B}, while remaining smooth on B).
The problem should be phrased as an open research question ('find' or 'can one find' a PDE proof), not as if the paper already contains such a proof.
To stay paper-faithful, the formulation should not broaden the class of admissible solutions beyond the smooth plurisubharmonic Dirichlet setting used in Theorem 3.1.
It should make explicit that the constant is C=C(n,p), independent of φ and f.
refined_question: Can one find a proof, using PDE techniques, of the following Kołodziej L^∞ a priori estimate? Let B ⊂ C^n be the unit ball and fix p>1. Suppose φ is plurisubharmonic, smooth on B and continuous on \bar{B}, with φ|_{∂B}=0, and satisfies det(φ_{j\bar{k}})=f in B, where φ_{j\bar{k}}=∂²φ/∂z_j∂\bar{z}_k and f∈L^p(B). Is it possible to prove by PDE methods alone that there exists a constant C=C(n,p)>0 such that ||φ||_{L^∞(B)} ≤ C ||f||_{L^p(B)}^{1/n}?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Section 3.1, Question 18, not a broader regularity problem. Theorem 3.1 states the precise estimate your draft reproduces, and the very next sentence says that no PDE proof is known; Question 18 then asks to find such a proof. So your draft is already very close in substance, but it needs to be reframed as the paper’s open problem and made fully stand-alone by spelling out the domain, equation, operator notation, norm convention, boundary trace, and parameter dependence of the constant.
